evidence: The architecture contract assigns Product One to existing Infinite Brutality owners: the real movement motor, input handlers, Rapier collision adapter, and a thin browser proof adapter.
The documented gap is a sequence-to-controller acceptance path; the target proof must replay the actual motor rather than introduce a second movement approximation.

Current controller-v1 tuning anchors jump charge, eye/body dimensions, ground acceleration and friction, walk/run speeds, run build, stick response, input smoothing, air steering/braking/drag, and collision radius.
The current runtime input record owns movement axes, smoothing, touch pointer identities, look state, gyro offsets, and jump charge state.
The current jump owner derives directional and vertical boosts from actual player velocity, move input, run state, and charge state.
The current device-event owner maps touch look/stick/jump, keyboard movement/jump, and optional gyro into the runtime input and camera state.
The floating-stick handlers position the touch surface, normalize displacement, apply the tuned response curve, and clear axes on release.
The current ground/air motor smooths input, builds run state, applies friction and acceleration, handles air turn/brake/drag and jump hold, then delegates motion to the Rapier adapter.
The collision owner creates the vendored Rapier world at 60 Hz and configures the character controller for sliding, autostep, ground snap, and slope limits.
The existing collision adapter registers deterministic cuboid proof geometry with source and kind ownership metadata.
The player-motion adapter computes character-controller movement, grounded state, contact metadata, and authoritative kinematic translation.
The existing arena candidate deterministically produces a floor, spawn, exit, and seeded generic cube field for isolated controller testing.
The current full-runtime candidate installs controller-kata state and realizes its floor, cubes, collision-backed walkable boxes, spawn, and exit beacon.

A thin standalone candidate already presents fixed-step movement, touch and keyboard input, Rapier collision, timing, and the seeded arena; it remains a candidate until shared controller-v1 ownership is proven.
The existing arena contract checks seeded repeatability, independence from ambient randomness, generic cube bounds, reserved spawn/exit regions, and JSON serialization.
The Product One suite currently labels the full-game player-climb source contract as its climb lane and reports that lane as PASS; this is not a direct bounded input-driven mantle proof.

The present climb contract reads main.js and player-climb.js and asserts source patterns for general climbing and mantling; it does not drive Product One input against a bounded obstacle or observe mantle completion.
The existing full-game climb owner selects terrain, authored-surface, and solid-wall attachment paths and enters a persistent climb state; this general climb system remains outside Product One.
The current controller proof builder realizes the floor, grid, 28 boxes, and exit, but this span contains no explicit bounded direct-mantle fixture or input-driven mantle acceptance path.

The corrected shared mantle owner rejects grounded or non-airborne approaches, requires positive jump velocity and actual wall-contact-normal facing, constrains feet-to-lip height, derives a clamped lip-relative inset target, requires support and body clearance, and caps displacement.
The existing full-game mantle updater now consumes the shared constrained interpolation result, keeps velocity zero during motion, and completes grounded without adding launch velocity.
The Rapier adapter validates the proposed landing against its registered cuboid collider records for source-owned top support and capsule clearance.

The authoritative controller records grounded approach readiness, passes real Rapier contacts, airborne velocity and camera facing into the shared constrained planner, never enters CLIMB, and records bounded start/completion evidence.

The deterministic contract reproduces grounded contact, proves it cannot activate, then drives a positive-velocity airborne Rapier contact and checks normal-facing, height window, lip-relative target, support, clearance, displacement caps, zero velocity, no repeat, and no CLIMB.
The global QA owner validates project-relative ignore globs, converts them to excluding Git pathspecs before tracked and untracked enumeration, and hashes only the same nonignored dirty inputs.
Gate receipts and changed-file selection consume the manifest ignore policy consistently while retaining HEAD, configuration, command, and engine implementation binding.
The Product One manifest excludes only unrelated project artifacts from Git enumeration while keeping src and the two playable HTML entries as runtime impact paths.
The bound case explicitly includes the shared controller, physics, mantle, arena, deterministic simulator, and exact imported Rapier and Three.js modules that can change its verdict.
The playable arena owner defines the low edge, continuous up/top/down stair run, separate tall ledge, constrained mantle ledge, and their safe scenario bounds as deterministic page data.
Arena generation keeps 28 seeded random boxes clear of the authored lane and returns the stable geometry hash, fixture records, scenarios, and direct-mantle alias.
The authoritative page renders and registers collision by iterating the exact traversal fixtures emitted by generateControllerArena, alongside the grid and random boxes.
The simulator imports the page arena, validates roles and scenario records, and mounts its floor and traversal fixture sizes and positions without local traversal geometry.
The observation fails on a withheld playable fixture, requires stair ascent and return to ground, and reports the arena owner, stable geometry hash, and exact fixture ids.
The current generator evolves structural candidates and persists BLOCKMAP/PIPE artifacts, judgments, receipts, and manifests; it emits no 3D mantle fixture or scenario records.
The current controller-arena adapter reads only arena.cubes, renders them as scattered boxes, and always returns REJECT; it is not a 3D mantle-course generator.
The current six-tool MCP surface has block compilation/generation/judgment/retrieval and pressure inspection, but no mantle-course tool.
The strict controller capability validator rejects unknown/missing/nonpositive fields, invalid relative reach ordering, and profiles whose ballistic jump cannot bring an above-eye lip into reach.

The mantle-course generator derives grounded-step, low-mantle, high-mantle, and impossible cuboids from the validated profile, emits approach/success scenario records and formula provenance, hashes the course, and optionally persists deterministic JSON plus data-only ESM.
The MCP server exposes the strict capability profile through generate_mantle_course as the seventh tool and returns the shared structured MCP response.
The playable arena imports the data-only Boxcraft course, pins its generator commit and course hash, and fails closed if schema, hash, or controller profile differ.
The arena retains 28 deterministic random cuboids, reserves the legacy and Boxcraft approach lanes, and returns the exact course fixtures and scenarios consumed by the page.
The immutable Product One profile owns eye height, radius, autostep, jump, gravity, relative mantle reach, and mantle-forward capabilities shared with the generated course.

Every real wall contact resolves through the physics cuboid owner, candidates sort deterministically, and an armed rising jump delegates contact-normal, reach, support, and clearance planning without a privileged fixture.
The physics adapter exposes an exact read-only walkable-cuboid lookup and rejects missing, terrain, solid, or non-cuboid sources.
The authoritative page exposes all pinned course records for capture and renders/registers collision by iterating the exact arena traversal fixtures and 28 random boxes.
The simulator imports the page arena and shared controller, validates the Boxcraft relations, and mounts the exact floor, traversal, and random-cuboid records.
The observation proves autostep, low/high/random mantle, impossible rejection, actual shared jump/contact ownership, zero completion velocity, no CLIMB, and exact mounted-record parity.
The bound data-only case pins the Boxcraft commit, course hash, exact Product One profile, arena geometry hash, 28 boxes, and qualifying seeded cube-12.
The checked-in data-only artifact pin records the canonical Boxcraft repository, generator commit, API, and course hash.
The shipped adapter is the single page-and-QA boundary for normalized movement, jump commit, and fixed-step controller updates, with traceable move/jump/step events.

The controller resolves real Rapier walkable-cuboid contacts, adapts the original constrained traversal acceptance region, delegates bounded support/clearance planning, and exposes only the shipped input adapter rather than a public queueJump bypass.
symbol: generic constrained mantle and public controller API

evidence: The playable spawn is derived from the pinned Boxcraft high-mantle scenario instead of leaving the target lateral to the default route.
Jump buttons and keyboard feed the shipped jump path without assigning the action pointer as the look pointer; movement keys remain the page input source.
Product One reuses the existing Infinite Brutality arms load, update, clear-depth, and render owners while combat and enemies stay excluded from the proof.

The harness mounts the actual arena and exercises the shipped adapter over partial-stick, angle, timing, and variable-frame domains; it rejects direct bypass and a safely contained out-of-contact jump without claiming visual acceptance.

The global engine generates deterministic domain boundaries/interiors, validates complete causal-edge packets, records append-only prospective receipts, and fails closed on unmapped mutations or stale engine/HEAD state.
The engine derives static HTML/ESM production and command graphs, rejects missing shipped adapters, injects the Node trace preload, and records actual executable, argv, and adapter events.
The aggregate engine suite arms a 90-second traceback-and-exit watchdog and cancels it only after the test class completes.
